objective: Fetching data with the Fetch API and handling JSON responses

sources.cite: Using the Fetch API, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2025-08-20)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: 'The promise returned by fetch() will reject on some errors, such as a network error or a bad scheme. However, if the server responds with an error like 404, then fetch() fulfills with a Response, so we have to check the status before we can read the response body'; 'A common pattern is to check the value of ok and throw if it is false'; json() 'will throw an exception if the response body is not in the appropriate format'.

sources.cite: Response: ok property, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2025-03-13)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: ok 'contains a Boolean stating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not'.

sources.cite: AbortSignal: timeout() static method, MDN Web Docs (last modified 2026-09-01)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-16. Relevant text: it 'returns an AbortSignal that will automatically abort after a specified time'; 'The signal will abort with its AbortSignal.reason property set to a TimeoutError DOMException on timeout'; the example passes { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000) } to fetch and checks err.name === "TimeoutError".

brief.situation: You maintain the teller rate board for Lakeside Credit Union (fictional), a page whose rates.js fetches today's rates from the internal rate service. Since 09:10 the service has been degraded, and twice this morning a branch board showed a 30-year fixed rate of 0.00%. The next deploy train leaves at 11:00. It is 10:15.
handover: The console is clean: whatever is going wrong is not being logged.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: open or profile something, run a query, a check or a test, change the code or the model, or ship the result. A cell marked with a pencil can be changed by picking a value. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
The console shows what is open, its flags, charts, tables and code, and the result of each step. 'Read the console' reads it aloud, and every chart can be shown as a table.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: fetch fulfills on an HTTP error status; json() then threw on the 503's HTML body; the catch returned {} and the render turned a missing rate into 0.00.
parts.modelAnswer: A 503 resolves the fetch; res.json() throws on '<html>'; catch returns {}; (undefined ?? 0).toFixed(2) is 0.00.

parts.label: What it does now
parts.criteria: Checks res.ok and throws with the status before parsing; the board says rates are unavailable and keeps the last good rates with their time; a timeout stops a hung request; no unbounded retry.
parts.modelAnswer: if (!res.ok) throw ...; banner with the 09:58 rates; AbortSignal.timeout(5000).

scoring.modelReasoning: fetch() fulfills with a Response even when the server answers 503; only network-level failures reject. The code called res.json() on the 503's HTML page, which threw, and a catch that returned {} let the render show 0.00%. Check res.ok (status 200-299) and throw with the status before parsing; on any failure show that rates are unavailable with the last good rates and their time; pass AbortSignal.timeout so a hung request ends with a TimeoutError. A retry loop with no limit floods a failing service. Test the failure path with a mocked 503.
